hook: The police **called me** to the station for questioning.

slides.title: Called as a witness? Some people **can't be made to go.**
slides.body: No male under 15 or above 60, no woman, and no mentally or physically disabled or acutely ill person can be required to attend anywhere other than where they live.

slides.title: But you **can choose** to go.
slides.body: If such a person is willing to attend the police station, they may be allowed to do so.

slides.title: Suspected of an offence? You may get **a notice.**
slides.body: If arrest isn't required, police must issue a notice to a person suspected of a cognizable offence to appear before them, or at a place named in the notice.

slides.title: Complying is **your duty.**
slides.body: Once you get such a notice, it's your duty to comply. If you do, and keep complying, you shall not be arrested for that offence unless police record reasons why you should be.

slides.title: Ignore it, and you **can be arrested.**
slides.body: If you fail to comply with the notice, or refuse to identify yourself, police may arrest you for the offence in the notice, subject to any court orders.

slides.title: You can't be **forced to testify against yourself.**
slides.body: The Constitution says no person accused of any offence shall be compelled to be a witness against himself.

sources: Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 – Section 35 (indiacode.nic.in), Section 179
MHA: Provisions for women and children in the new criminal laws (pib.gov.in)
caption:
Police called you in for questioning? Here's what the law says. 👇

1️⃣ As a witness, a male under 15 or above 60, a woman, or a disabled or acutely ill person can't be required to attend anywhere other than where they live
2️⃣ They can still choose to go to the police station
3️⃣ Suspected of a cognizable offence and arrest isn't needed? Police must give you a notice to appear, and complying is your duty
4️⃣ Comply, and you shall not be arrested unless police record reasons. Ignore it, and you can be arrested
5️⃣ No person accused of an offence can be compelled to be a witness against himself

Source: Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 – Sections 35, 179; Constitution of India – Article 20(3); MHA
